addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

attachment.content:
- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

=============== aria-chart-role-img.yaml
title: 'feat(aria): add `role="img"` to chart container element'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Assistive technologies need a semantic hint that the chart container represents an image-like graphic region rather than an untyped generic element. Without that role, accessibility support is weaker even when aria labeling is enabled.


  ## Desired outcome

  Mark the chart container with `role="img"` so screen readers can interpret the rendered chart as a descriptive graphical object and pair it with the existing aria text more reliably.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A rendered chart container exposes `role="img"`, existing aria-label behavior continues to work on the same element, and visual rendering is unchanged.'
=============== aria-label-data-exclusion.yaml
title: 'feat(aria): allows excluding data in aria-label'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Accessible chart descriptions can become noisy when datasets include raw coordinates, identifiers, or helper columns that are meaningful for computation but not for screen-reader output. Authors need a way to omit specific dimensions while keeping the underlying data intact.


  ## Desired outcome

  Let aria label generation exclude selected dataset columns through `aria.label.data.excludeDimensionId`, so spoken descriptions can focus on the meaningful values without mutating the actual series data.


  ## Acceptance signals

  When `aria.label.data.excludeDimensionId` lists dimension indexes, those values are omitted from the generated aria label, the remaining values still appear in order, and reading back the series data shows it was not modified by aria generation.'

=============== aria-label-data-exclusion.yaml
title: 'feat(aria): allows excluding data in aria-label'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Accessible chart descriptions can become noisy when datasets include raw coordinates, identifiers, or helper columns that are meaningful for computation but not for screen-reader output. Authors need a way to omit specific dimensions while keeping the underlying data intact.


  ## Desired outcome

  Let aria label generation exclude selected dataset columns through `aria.label.data.excludeDimensionId`, so spoken descriptions can focus on the meaningful values without mutating the actual series data.


  ## Acceptance signals

  When `aria.label.data.excludeDimensionId` lists dimension indexes, those values are omitted from the generated aria label, the remaining values still appear in order, and reading back the series data shows it was not modified by aria generation.'
=============== aria-ssr-safety.yaml
title: 'fix(aria): avoid throwing error in SSR mode'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Teams using ECharts for server-side rendering or prerendered output expect accessibility features to be safe to enable outside the browser. Right now aria processing can throw in SSR environments because DOM-only behavior is assumed even when no browser element exists.


  ## Desired outcome

  Make aria support safe in SSR mode so enabling accessibility metadata does not crash chart generation when ECharts is rendered without a live browser DOM.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Charts configured with aria can be created in server-rendered environments without throwing, browser rendering keeps its current accessibility behavior, and the fix does not require users to disable aria as a workaround.'
=============== aria-test-20218.yaml
title: 'test(aria): fix test case of #20218'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  The automated coverage for aria column exclusion needs to reflect the public option structure that users are supposed to configure. This is test-maintenance work, not a change to chart behavior.


  ## Desired outcome

  Update the regression test so it validates the supported public contract at `aria.label.data.excludeDimensionId`, while keeping the existing user-facing aria behavior and data-integrity expectations unchanged.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The regression test exercises `aria.label.data.excludeDimensionId`, still confirms excluded columns disappear from the generated aria label, still confirms source data is left untouched, and no runtime feature change is introduced by the test update itself.'
=============== axis-custom-values.yaml
title: 'feat(axis): add `customValues` option to customize axis tick/label positions'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Chart authors sometimes need ticks and labels at hand-picked positions rather than at the axis scale’s automatically generated stops, for example when highlighting irregular milestones or business-specific checkpoints. Today this usually requires workarounds that can desynchronize labels from ticks.


  ## Desired outcome

  Allow both axis ticks and axis labels to opt into explicit positions through `customValues`, so authors can declare the exact values to show while still using the normal axis rendering pipeline.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Providing `customValues` on the tick or label configuration renders marks at the requested values, time axes handle those custom positions correctly, and charts that rely on automatic tick generation keep their current behavior.'
=============== axis-ticks-grid-overflow.yaml
title: 'fix(axis): fix ticks overflowing grid area with dataZoom'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  When dataZoom is applied, axis ticks near the visible edges can extend beyond the grid area and make a chart look visually broken even though the zoomed range itself is valid. Authors expect clipped or bounded ticks that stay inside the plotting region.


  ## Desired outcome

  Keep axis ticks contained within the grid when dataZoom changes the visible window, so zoomed charts look clean at the edges instead of drawing tick marks outside the plot area.


  ## Acceptance signals

  After zooming, edge ticks no longer overflow beyond the grid boundary, normal axis-tick rendering is preserved inside the plot, and unaffected non-zoomed charts keep their current appearance.'
=============== bar-bordercolor-large-data.yaml
title: 'fix(bar): fix borderColor hides bar color with large data'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Large bar-series rendering can lose the bar fill when `borderColor` is configured, making bars appear incorrectly outlined or visually empty. This is especially noticeable in dense charts where the large-data path is chosen automatically.


  ## Desired outcome

  Fix the large-data bar rendering path so `borderColor` does not hide the bar’s actual fill color.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Bars rendered through the large-data path keep their fill color even when `borderColor` is set, border styling still applies as expected, and standard bar rendering remains unchanged.'
=============== bigint-data-handling.yaml
title: 'fix(data): avoid crashing with BigInt values'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Some chart authors pass data that includes JavaScript `BigInt` values from upstream business logic or preprocessing steps. Instead of gracefully interpreting or rejecting that input, ECharts can crash during value detection and parsing, taking down the whole chart render.


  ## Desired outcome

  Make data ingestion robust when `BigInt` values are present so charts no longer throw during value parsing, and users can either render supported numeric content or get normal downstream handling instead of a hard crash.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Supplying data that contains `BigInt` no longer causes an immediate exception in the parsing pipeline, and other supported numeric data paths continue to behave exactly as before.'
=============== boxplot-encode-category-axis.yaml
title: 'fix(boxplot): correctly handle `series.encode` with category axis'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Boxplot charts can be driven from datasets and `series.encode`, but when a category axis is involved the encoded dimensions may be interpreted incorrectly. The result is a valid option that renders with misplaced or missing statistical boxes.


  ## Desired outcome

  Make boxplot series honor `series.encode` correctly on category axes so dataset-driven configurations map categories and box statistics to the intended dimensions.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A boxplot backed by dataset plus `series.encode` renders the expected categories and box values on a category axis, the encoded mapping no longer breaks the series, and existing boxplots without encode keep their current behavior.'
=============== calendar-label-silent.yaml
title: 'feat(calendar): add `silent` option for `dayLabel`/`monthLabel`/`yearLabel`'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  A chart author using the calendar coordinate system may want the day, month, or year labels to serve as static annotation rather than interactive elements. Today those labels still participate in pointer interaction, which can interfere with hover behavior on the actual calendar data and make embedded dashboards feel unexpectedly clickable.

  ## Desired outcome

  Calendar label interaction should be configurable independently for `dayLabel`, `monthLabel`, and `yearLabel`. When a user sets `silent: true` on any of those label configs, the corresponding rendered text should ignore pointer events while preserving the existing visual styling and positioning.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Authors can set `dayLabel.silent`, `monthLabel.silent`, and `yearLabel.silent` directly in the calendar option, and each one takes effect on its own. With `silent: true`, the label remains visible but no longer behaves like an interactive graphic element; with the option omitted or false, existing behavior stays unchanged.

  '
=============== candlestick-non-normal-states.yaml
title: 'fix(candlestick): add back missing support for non-normal states since v5.0.0'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Candlestick charts support emphasis, blur, and select-style visual states, and users expect those non-normal states to continue working consistently across major versions. Since v5.0.0 some of that state handling was lost, so interactive styling no longer responds correctly.


  ## Desired outcome

  Restore the missing non-normal state support for candlestick series so hover, selection, and related state-based visuals behave again the way chart authors expect.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Candlestick items respond correctly in non-normal states, state-specific styling takes effect again without breaking normal rendering, and existing candlestick options keep their prior semantics.'
=============== custom-renderitem-compoundpath.yaml
title: 'feat(custom): support compoundPath in custom series renderItem'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Custom-series authors sometimes need to return a composed path made from several subpaths as a single logical drawing element. Today `compoundPath` is not supported in `renderItem`, which blocks reusable vector shapes that are straightforward in lower-level graphics APIs.


  ## Desired outcome

  Support `compoundPath` as a valid custom-series element type so `renderItem` can return grouped path geometry in one element definition, provided `shape.paths` is supplied.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A custom series can return a `compoundPath` element from `renderItem`, `shape.paths` is honored when constructing the final graphic, and invalid compound definitions still fail clearly instead of silently misrendering.'
=============== custom-series-installer.yaml
title: 'feat(custom): use installer for reusable custom series'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Reusable custom series should integrate like other chart types so wrapper libraries and modular builds can register them through the standard installation flow. This is an API ergonomics improvement for developers building on top of ECharts.


  ## Desired outcome

  Provide installer-based registration for reusable custom series so they can be added through the normal modular setup path rather than special-case wiring.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A reusable custom series can be registered through the standard installer flow, modular imports stay consistent with other chart features, and existing custom-series usage keeps working.'
=============== dark-legend-page-text.yaml
title: 'fix(theme): fix legend page text color in dark mode'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  In dark mode, legend pagination text can retain an incorrect color that reduces contrast and readability against the theme background. Users experience this as a theme inconsistency in otherwise polished dark dashboards.


  ## Desired outcome

  Fix dark-theme legend page text coloring so paged legends remain readable and visually consistent with the rest of the dark theme.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Legend page text in dark mode uses an appropriate readable color, pagination controls stay visible against the dark background, and light-theme behavior is unchanged.'
=============== datazoom-handlelabel-show.yaml
title: 'feat(dataZoom): new option handleLabel.show'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Slider dataZoom handles can show useful value text while users interact, but some applications want those handle labels visible even outside active dragging or emphasis states. At the moment authors cannot explicitly control that visibility.


  ## Desired outcome

  Introduce `handleLabel.show` for slider dataZoom so teams can decide whether the handle labels are visible in the normal state, while `emphasis.handleLabel.show` continues to control the emphasized or dragging state separately.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Setting `handleLabel.show` toggles normal-state handle-label visibility, `emphasis.handleLabel.show` governs the emphasized state, and existing slider behavior is preserved when the new option is left unset.'
=============== datazoom-movehandler-cursor.yaml
title: 'fix(dataZoom): change moveHandler cursor to default'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  The move handle in dataZoom currently presents a cursor that implies a stronger drag affordance than the interaction actually intends in that state. This creates small but noticeable UX inconsistency in the control.


  ## Desired outcome

  Use the default cursor for the move handler so pointer feedback matches the intended interaction model without changing the rest of dataZoom behavior.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Hovering the move handler shows the default cursor, dragging behavior stays available where it was before, and no other slider handle cursor states regress.'
=============== forked-workflow-deps.yaml
title: 'chore(workflow): use forked workflow deps for timely update'
category: ci
requirement: '## Context

  Project maintainers need the CI workflows that power preview and maintenance tasks to stay updateable without waiting on external bottlenecks. This is internal release-engineering work rather than a user-facing feature.


  ## Desired outcome

  Adjust the workflow dependency source so maintainers can receive updates in a timely way while keeping the observable behavior of preview-related automation unchanged for contributors.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The workflows continue to run with the replacement dependency source, update cadence is no longer blocked in the old path, and no charting API or runtime behavior changes for users.'
=============== gauge-negative-z2.yaml
title: 'fix(gauge): fix z2 is negative when maxVal is negative'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Gauge charts may calculate drawing order from the maximum value, and when that maximum is negative the resulting `z2` can become negative as well. Users see this as incorrect stacking or visibility problems even though negative-value gauges are a legitimate configuration.


  ## Desired outcome

  Make gauge rendering robust for negative maxima so internal z-ordering stays valid and the gauge remains visible and layered correctly.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A gauge configured with a negative max value renders without hidden or mislayered elements, `z2` no longer falls into an invalid negative ordering state, and positive-value gauges behave as before.'
=============== geojson-region-styling-2.yaml
title: 'feat(geo): support styling region in original GeoJSON data'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Chart authors need region defaults embedded in GeoJSON to work consistently whether they use a standalone `geo` component or a `series.map`, and whether or not they explicitly list every region in `data` or `regions`. The initial GeoJSON styling support still leaves gaps in those map-series flows, especially when a region only exists in the source map and not in user-supplied series data.

  ## Desired outcome

  GeoJSON-defined region styling should become a first-class default across map usage, not just a geo-view special case. If a feature provides `properties.echartsStyle`, that style should flow into both `geo.regions` and `series.map` region models, including regions that need to be synthesized into the data so name-based lookup, rendering, and labels all remain complete.

  ## Acceptance signals

  A `series.map` can pick up `properties.echartsStyle` from the original GeoJSON even when the author did not manually add a matching data item for that region. The style participates in the normal region model pipeline instead of being a one-off view patch, so map rendering, labels, and region lookup stay consistent with other region options.

  '
=============== geojson-region-styling.yaml
title: 'feat(geo): support styling region in original GeoJSON data'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Teams who maintain their own GeoJSON files often want the map source itself to carry default presentation rules for specific regions, instead of forcing every chart option to restate those styles. At the moment, styling embedded directly in the GeoJSON is ignored, which makes shared map assets harder to reuse across multiple visualizations.

  ## Desired outcome

  When a GeoJSON region includes an `echartsStyle` property in its feature properties, ECharts should treat that as the region''s default styling for geo rendering. This should let authors ship map-specific visual defaults inside the original GeoJSON while still allowing chart configuration to build on top of those defaults where appropriate.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Region-level styles declared in GeoJSON `properties.echartsStyle` are reflected when the map is rendered through geo-based views, without requiring duplicate style configuration in every chart option. Existing GeoJSON files that do not define `echartsStyle` continue to render exactly as before.

  '
=============== georoam-totalzoom-event.yaml
title: 'feat(geo): add `totalZoom` parameter for the `georoam` event'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Applications that react to map zooming often need the cumulative zoom level, not just the latest roam gesture, in order to coordinate labels, overlays, or linked views. Today a `georoam` listener can detect that roaming happened but cannot directly read the total scale after repeated zoom operations.


  ## Desired outcome

  Expose the accumulated zoom ratio on the `georoam` event as `totalZoom` so integrators can base follow-up UI logic on the map’s current effective zoom level instead of reconstructing it themselves.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A `georoam` handler receives `totalZoom` after zoom interactions, the value tracks cumulative zoom state across successive operations, and existing roam event behavior continues to work for listeners that do not use the new field.'
=============== inversed-time-bandwidth.yaml
title: 'fix(axis): fix bar bandWidth with inversed time axis'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Bar charts on an inversed time axis can calculate the wrong `bandWidth`, which causes bar sizing and spacing to look off even when the input data and axis configuration are otherwise correct. Authors experience this as distorted geometry on a valid timeline chart.


  ## Desired outcome

  Correct bar bandwidth calculation for inversed time axes so bar width matches the actual axis interval direction and the rendered bars keep sensible spacing.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Bars on an inversed time axis render with the expected width, reversing the axis no longer distorts band sizing, and non-inversed time-axis bar charts keep their current layout.'
=============== legend-action-isolation.yaml
title: 'fix(legend): fix legend action is not isolated from other legend components'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Pages can contain multiple legend components, and actions intended for one legend should not silently affect another. Right now some legend operations leak across legend instances, causing unexpected selection changes elsewhere in the same chart.


  ## Desired outcome

  Isolate legend actions so each legend component responds only to the interactions and action payloads meant for it, even when several legends coexist in one option.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Triggering an action on one legend no longer changes unrelated legend components, targeted legend interaction still works, and existing single-legend charts behave the same as before.'
=============== line-memory-reduction.yaml
title: 'perf(line): reduce runtime memory cost'
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  Large line charts can put unnecessary pressure on the browser by holding more runtime memory than the renderer actually needs. Users feel this as slower interaction or higher memory usage rather than as a visible API problem.


  ## Desired outcome

  Reduce the runtime memory footprint of line-series rendering without changing chart appearance, public options, or event behavior.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Equivalent line charts consume less memory during rendering or interaction, visual output remains unchanged, and no public configuration changes are required from chart authors.'
=============== linked-data-npe.yaml
title: 'fix(series): avoid NPE caused by `seriesData.getLinkedData`'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Advanced charts and extensions can interact with linked data structures internally, but some series configurations hit a null-path and throw when linked data is absent. Users experience this as a broken render caused by an internal assumption rather than an invalid option they knowingly supplied.


  ## Desired outcome

  Harden series processing so code paths that consult `seriesData.getLinkedData` tolerate missing linked datasets and continue rendering safely instead of raising a null-pointer-style exception.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Series configurations that previously crashed due to missing linked data now render or degrade normally, no exception is thrown from the linked-data lookup path, and unaffected series behavior stays the same.'
=============== map-regions-silent.yaml
title: 'feat(map): support `regions[].silent` and update map data in tests'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Map authors sometimes need a region to remain visible but non-interactive, for example when a background territory should not respond to hover, selection, or tooltip behavior. ECharts already supports top-level `silent` behavior, but there is no reliable per-region contract for map and geo regions, so authors cannot selectively disable interaction on individual areas.

  ## Desired outcome

  Region configuration should support `silent` at the per-region level through `regions[].silent`, and that setting should be honored for both geo-based maps and `series.map` rendering. A region marked silent should keep its visual appearance while opting out of event handling and interactive affordances, without forcing the entire map to become non-interactive.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Authors can declare `silent` on individual entries in `regions`, and the targeted region becomes non-interactive while neighboring regions continue to respond normally. The contract applies consistently to rendered GeoJSON regions and SVG-backed regions, and map data refreshes should preserve the updated region behavior instead of losing it when the source map data changes.

  '
=============== marker-formatter-series-context.yaml
title: 'fix(marker): fix marker label formatter can''t get series information'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  When chart authors customize marker labels with formatter callbacks, they expect to receive the same series context that other formatter-based APIs expose. For mark points, lines, and areas, that context can currently be incomplete, which prevents formatter logic from reliably reading series information.


  ## Desired outcome

  Ensure marker label formatter callbacks receive the related series metadata consistently so custom label text can depend on the originating series without hacks or duplicated state.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A marker label formatter can read the expected series information when building label text, the callback contract is consistent across marker types, and existing marker rendering remains unchanged when no custom formatter is used.'
=============== markline-symboloffset-2d-array.yaml
title: 'fix(type): markLine `symbolOffset` can be a 2d array for both symbols'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  TypeScript users configuring mark lines may want separate offsets for the symbols at each end, but the current type definition can reject valid configurations even though the renderer supports them. This creates unnecessary friction in strongly typed projects.


  ## Desired outcome

  Update the public type contract so markLine `symbolOffset` accepts a 2D array when authors need to specify offsets for both symbols independently.


  ## Acceptance signals

  TypeScript accepts markLine configurations where `symbolOffset` is expressed as separate offset pairs for the two end symbols, existing simpler `symbolOffset` forms remain valid, and runtime chart behavior is unchanged.'
=============== master-into-v6.yaml
title: 'chore: merge master into v6'
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  The v6 release branch needs regular synchronization with ongoing master development so maintainers can keep packaging, fixes, and infrastructure aligned. This is branch-management work, not a new user-visible feature.


  ## Desired outcome

  Merge the relevant master changes into the v6 branch while preserving the expected public behavior of the release line and avoiding regressions introduced by branch drift.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The v6 branch reflects the intended upstream updates, the merge does not invent a new standalone feature requirement of its own, and user-facing behavior is whatever the merged source already defines.'
=============== minmax-sampling-behavior.yaml
title: 'fix(sample): fix minmax sampling behaviour'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Users relying on `minmax` sampling expect the downsampled line to preserve the local extrema from each interval. In some cases the current behavior picks the wrong points, so the sampled chart misrepresents the highs and lows of the underlying data.


  ## Desired outcome

  Fix `minmax` sampling so the reduced series preserves the intended minimum and maximum behavior within each sampling bucket, especially around edge cases where the previous logic selected the wrong point order or values.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A line using `minmax` sampling retains the visible peaks and troughs expected from the source data, the sampled output is stable in the previously failing scenario, and other sampling modes continue to behave as before.'
=============== npm-package-ignore-files.yaml
title: 'chore: ignore some unused dirs and files from npm'
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  Package consumers install ECharts from npm and only need the distributable assets required to use or bundle the library. Extra repository-only folders in the published package add noise and increase install size without adding user value.


  ## Desired outcome

  Tighten the npm package contents so development-only material that is not needed by downstream users is left out, while the package continues to install and work exactly the same for chart authors.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The published package excludes unnecessary repo artifacts, npm installs stay smaller and cleaner, and existing runtime and type-consumption behavior is unchanged for consumers.'
=============== pictorial-zero-value-flipping.yaml
title: 'fix(pictorial): fix zero value flipping for different axes'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  A chart author using `pictorialBar` with image or path symbols expects zero-valued items to stay visually anchored without suddenly mirroring in the wrong direction. After the earlier zero-value fix, some axis combinations still render a flipped symbol when the chart changes between horizontal and vertical layouts or uses inverse axes, so the same data can look wrong depending on orientation.

  ## Desired outcome

  Zero-valued pictorial bars should keep a stable, sensible symbol direction across horizontal and vertical charts, including inverse-axis layouts. A value of zero must no longer trigger an accidental flip simply because the axis orientation or inversion changes.

  ## Acceptance signals

  The zero-value rendering is correct for all four combinations covered by chart authors in practice: horizontal, horizontal with inverse axis, vertical, and vertical with inverse axis. Non-zero pictorial bars continue to render with their existing direction logic, and the fix applies equally to custom image symbols and path-based symbols.

  '
=============== pictorialbar-zero-symbol-flip.yaml
title: 'fix(pictorialBar): symbol should not flip with zero data'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Pictorial bar charts can use symbol direction and orientation to express meaning, but a zero value should not invert that symbol unexpectedly. Right now hitting zero can flip the symbol, producing a misleading visual jump at exactly the point where no bar should extend.


  ## Desired outcome

  Keep pictorial-bar symbols from flipping when the data value is zero so orientation stays stable across zero-valued points.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A zero-value pictorial bar preserves the expected symbol direction, nearby positive or negative values still render with their intended orientation rules, and zero no longer introduces a special-case flip.'

category: bugfix

596	requirement: '## Context
597	
598	  The release branch needs to stay aligned with ongoing mainline work without changing the already-shipped contracts in surprising ways. This merge is repository maintenance rather than a discrete user-facing feature request.
599	
600	
601	  ## Desired outcome
602	
603	  Bring the release branch back in sync with the current master branch contents while preserving the intended public behavior of the v6 line and avoiding accidental regressions in packaging, types, or chart rendering.
604	
605	
606	  ## Acceptance signals
607	
608	  The branch contains the expected upstream changes after the merge, no standalone new requirement is introduced beyond synchronization itself, and public behavior remains the one defined by the merged source.'
609	=============== release-v5-6-0.yaml
610	title: Release v5.6.0
611	category: other
612	requirement: '## Context
613	
614	  ECharts is ready for its 5.6.0 release and downstream users need a publishable package that reflects the latest completed work across chart behavior, geo/map handling, visualMap interaction, rendering fixes, and localization assets. This is release engineering rather than a new end-user feature, but it is the step that turns the accumulated changes into something consumers can install and ship.
615	
616	  ## Desired outcome
617	
618	  Prepare the 5.6.0 release so the distributed bundles, package metadata, and generated assets all match the current source state. The published package should identify itself as version `5.6.0`, depend on `zrender` `5.6.1`, and include the newly generated locale bundles such as `langFA` and `langSV`, while preserving the user-visible behavior delivered by the merged fixes and features in this release.
619	
620	  ## Acceptance signals
621	
622	  The release artifacts and package metadata are internally consistent for version `5.6.0`, the generated distribution files are rebuilt from current sources, and the added locale bundles are available to consumers in the shipped package. This remains a packaging and release update, so no previously documented public API or runtime behavior should regress beyond the intentional changes already included in the release.
623	
624	  '
625	=============== reusable-custom-series.yaml
626	title: 'feat(custom): reusable custom series'
627	category: feature
628	requirement: '## Context
629	
630	  Teams building reusable custom series often need to pass shared context into every `renderItem` invocation without recomputing or closing over external mutable state. Today there is no first-class channel for that reusable payload.
631	
632	
633	  ## Desired outcome
634	
635	  Support a reusable payload on custom series through `itemPayload`, and expose the same object on `renderItem` params so extensions and higher-level wrappers can share contextual data cleanly across item rendering.
636	
637	
638	  ## Acceptance signals
639	
640	  A custom series can declare `itemPayload`, each `renderItem` call receives that payload through `params.itemPayload`, and existing custom-series rendering keeps working when no payload is provided.'
641	=============== roamcontrollerhost-import-path.yaml
642	title: 'fix(roam): fix RoamControllerHost importing path'
643	category: bugfix
644	requirement: '## Context
645	
646	  Projects that compile or consume ECharts internals need its roam helper host type to resolve from the correct module path. A bad import path is not a product feature bug, but it can break builds and downstream integration work.
647	
648	
649	  ## Desired outcome
650	
651	  Correct the `RoamControllerHost` import path so the relevant code compiles and resolves cleanly without changing any runtime roaming behavior.
652	
653	
654	  ## Acceptance signals
655	
656	  The affected module builds without path-resolution errors, `RoamControllerHost` is imported from the correct public location, and chart interaction behavior remains unchanged.'
657	=============== sankey-border-radius.yaml
658	title: 'feat(sankey): add `itemStyle.borderRadius` option for sankey series'
659	category: feature
660	requirement: '## Context
661	
662	  Designers using sankey diagrams can control node colors and borders, but the nodes still render with sharp corners even in interfaces that otherwise use rounded visual language. This makes sankey charts harder to match with surrounding product styling.
663	
664	
665	  ## Desired outcome
666	
667	  Allow sankey series styling to honor `itemStyle.borderRadius` so node rectangles can render with rounded corners when authors opt in, while existing charts keep their current appearance by default.
668	
669	
670	  ## Acceptance signals
671	
672	  Setting `itemStyle.borderRadius` on a sankey series produces visibly rounded node corners, the option behaves like other ECharts radius-style controls, and leaving it unset preserves the current rectangular rendering.'
673	=============== sankey-undefined-options.yaml
674	title: 'fix(sankey): avoid throwing errors when the `links` / `nodes` / `levels` option is undefined'
675	category: bugfix
676	requirement: '## Context
677	
678	  Applications sometimes build sankey options incrementally, and optional arrays such as `links`, `nodes`, or `levels` may be undefined until later. ECharts should not crash just because those optional fields are temporarily absent.
679	
680	
681	  ## Desired outcome
682	
683	  Handle missing sankey `links`, `nodes`, and `levels` inputs defensively so the chart no longer throws when those option fields are undefined.
684	
685	
686	  ## Acceptance signals
687	
688	  A sankey option with undefined `links`, `nodes`, or `levels` no longer raises an exception, normal sankey rendering still works when those arrays are provided, and authors do not need to add dummy empty arrays solely to avoid crashes.'
689	=============== seriesdata-rawindexof-npe.yaml
690	title: 'fix(data): fix potential NPE in the `SeriesData#rawIndexOf` function'
691	category: bugfix
692	requirement: '## Context
693	
694	  A developer using ECharts internals or extension code can end up calling `SeriesData#rawIndexOf` in situations where the requested dimension does not have an inverted index. Instead of failing gracefully, that lookup can crash the chart pipeline with a null-pointer style error before the caller has any chance to recover.
695	
696	  ## Desired outcome
697	
698	  `SeriesData#rawIndexOf` should be safe to call even when the requested dimension is missing from the inverted-index map. In that case it should behave like an unsuccessful lookup rather than a hard failure, so downstream code can continue handling the result normally.
699	
700	  ## Acceptance signals
701	
702	  Calling `SeriesData#rawIndexOf` with a dimension that has no inverted index must not throw in production execution. The method should return the same "not found" result it already uses for missing values, namely `INDEX_NOT_FOUND`, so callers see a consistent contract instead of an exception.
703	
704	  '
705	=============== splitline-min-max-lines.yaml
706	title: 'feat(axis): add `showMinLine` / `showMaxLine` option for `splitLine`'
707	category: feature
708	requirement: '## Context
709	
710	  Some designs need axis split lines only at the lower bound, upper bound, or both boundary lines, especially in compact dashboards where every extra grid line adds clutter. Today authors cannot express that boundary-only behavior directly.
711	
712	
713	  ## Desired outcome
714	
715	  Add `showMinLine` and `showMaxLine` to split-line configuration so chart authors can independently control whether the minimum and maximum boundary lines are rendered.
716	
717	
718	  ## Acceptance signals
719	
720	  Turning on `showMinLine` or `showMaxLine` renders only the requested boundary split lines, existing split-line behavior remains unchanged when the options are absent, and authors can combine them for both ends when needed.'
721	=============== stepped-line-area-nulls.yaml
722	title: 'fix(line): fix areaStyle skewing in stepped line series and incorrect connectNull behavior'
723	category: bugfix
724	requirement: '## Context
725	
726	  Stepped line charts with area fills can render distorted polygons, and series that combine stepped lines with null data may connect points in ways authors did not intend. The result is a visibly wrong chart even though the series option is valid.
727	
728	
729	  ## Desired outcome
730	
731	  Fix stepped line rendering so `areaStyle` follows the step geometry correctly and `connectNull` respects gaps in the same way users expect from the stepped path, including edge cases where null values sit near step transitions.
732	
733	
734	  ## Acceptance signals
735	
736	  A stepped line with `areaStyle` no longer shows skewed fill geometry, null gaps are connected only when `connectNull` should apply, and the stepped series path stays visually consistent with its data order.'
737	=============== sunburst-relative-focus.yaml
738	title: 'feat(sunburst): add new emphasis focus strategy `''relative''` for highlighting ancestor and descendant nodes'
739	category: feature
740	requirement: '## Context
741	
742	  Sunburst emphasis controls are useful for focusing attention, but existing focus modes do not cover the common case where an application wants to highlight both a selected node’s ancestors and descendants together. Authors currently have to approximate that behavior externally.
743	
744	
745	  ## Desired outcome
746	
747	  Add a new sunburst emphasis focus mode named `relative` so hovering or emphasizing a node can highlight its surrounding family context, including both ancestor and descendant nodes, in one built-in strategy.
748	
749	
750	  ## Acceptance signals
751	
752	  Setting the sunburst emphasis focus strategy to `relative` highlights the target node together with its ancestors and descendants, other focus strategies keep their current semantics, and charts that do not use the new mode are unchanged.'
753	=============== time-meridian-template.yaml
754	title: 'feat(time): add meridian template {a}/{A}'
755	category: feature
756	requirement: '## Context
757	
758	  Chart authors formatting time labels and tooltips often need 12-hour clock output with an am/pm marker, especially for business dashboards and localized displays. ECharts time templates currently provide numeric hour fields but no direct meridian token, forcing users to post-process strings outside the formatter.
759	
760	
761	  ## Desired outcome
762	
763	  Add native meridian placeholders to the time formatter so templates can use `{a}` for lowercase `am` or `pm` and `{A}` for uppercase `AM` or `PM`, alongside the existing date and time tokens.
764	
765	
766	  ## Acceptance signals
767	
768	  Formatting a morning timestamp with `{a}` yields `am` and with `{A}` yields `AM`, afternoon timestamps switch to `pm` and `PM`, and the existing time-template placeholders continue to render unchanged.'
769	=============== tooltip-legend-name-xss.yaml
770	title: 'fix(tooltip): fix tooltip XSS issue when legend name is HTML string'
771	category: bugfix
772	requirement: '## Context
773	
774	  Applications often display user-provided legend names, and tooltip output must treat those names as content rather than executable markup. Right now an HTML string used as a legend name can flow into the tooltip in a way that creates an XSS risk.
775	
776	
777	  ## Desired outcome
778	
779	  Tooltip rendering should safely display legend names even when the text contains HTML-like characters, so user-facing charts show the intended label without interpreting it as active markup or script content.
780	
781	
782	  ## Acceptance signals
783	
784	  A legend name containing HTML is shown as plain text inside the tooltip, unsafe markup is not executed, and normal tooltip formatting still works for ordinary legend labels.'
785	=============== tooltip-lineheight-default.yaml
786	title: 'fix(tooltip): Tooltip textStyle lineHeight does not work in default '
787	category: bugfix
788	requirement: '## Context
789	
790	  Tooltip text styles support `lineHeight`, but in the default tooltip path that setting may be ignored, leading to cramped multi-line content even when authors explicitly configure spacing. This makes richly formatted tooltips harder to read.
791	
792	
793	  ## Desired outcome
794	
795	  Honor tooltip `textStyle.lineHeight` in the default tooltip rendering path so multi-line tooltip content respects the configured vertical spacing.
796	
797	
798	  ## Acceptance signals
799	
800	  A tooltip configured with `textStyle.lineHeight` shows the requested line spacing in the default renderer, multi-line content becomes more readable, and existing tooltip text styling continues to work alongside the new spacing behavior.'
801	=============== tooltip-notmerge-npe.yaml
802	title: 'fix(tooltip): fix potential NPE when setting option with `notMerge` strategy'
803	category: bugfix
804	requirement: '## Context
805	
806	  Applications that refresh chart options with `notMerge` expect tooltip infrastructure to reset cleanly between renders. Instead, the tooltip HTML layer can hit a null path during repositioning and throw an exception.
807	
808	
809	  ## Desired outcome
810	
811	  Make tooltip HTML handling resilient when options are replaced with `notMerge`, so rerendering does not trigger a null-pointer-style failure during size or position updates.
812	
813	
814	  ## Acceptance signals
815	
816	  Calling `setOption` with `notMerge` no longer crashes tooltip logic, tooltip positioning still works after rerender, and unaffected tooltip behavior remains unchanged.'
817	=============== treemap-custom-cursor.yaml
818	title: 'feature(treemap): add custom cursor properties for treemap'
819	category: feature
820	requirement: '## Context
821	
822	  Treemap authors often use pointer feedback to signal which nodes are clickable or drillable, but treemap nodes do not currently expose the same cursor customization that other interactive series can use. This makes clickable treemaps feel inconsistent in complex dashboards.
823	
824	
825	  ## Desired outcome

827	  Allow treemap node styling to specify `cursor` so authors can control the pointer shown over individual treemap content when interaction is available.

829	
830	  ## Acceptance signals
831	
832	  Setting `cursor` on treemap node configuration changes the cursor over the rendered node content, interactive nodes can visibly distinguish themselves from static ones, and charts that omit the option keep the current cursor behavior.'
833	=============== types-shared-import-path.yaml
834	title: 'fix(types): fix `import(''echarts/types/dist/shared'')` in users'' .d.ts can not visit `''echarts/types/dist/shared.d.ts''` since v5.5.0'

Since v5.5.0 that path is no longer reachable as expected, which breaks downstream `.d.ts` consumption even though the types still exist in the package.

849	=============== typescript-35-compatibility-tests.yaml

If the DTS test workflow only exercises older compiler versions, newer users can hit regressions that were never validated.

865	=============== visualmap-disabled-pointer-cursor.yaml

=============== aria-chart-role-img.yaml
title: 'feat(aria): add `role="img"` to chart container element'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Assistive technologies need a semantic hint that the chart container represents an image-like graphic region rather than an untyped generic element. Without that role, accessibility support is weaker even when aria labeling is enabled.


  ## Desired outcome

  Mark the chart container with `role="img"` so screen readers can interpret the rendered chart as a descriptive graphical object and pair it with the existing aria text more reliably.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A rendered chart container exposes `role="img"`, existing aria-label behavior continues to work on the same element, and visual rendering is unchanged.'
=============== aria-label-data-exclusion.yaml
title: 'feat(aria): allows excluding data in aria-label'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Accessible chart descriptions can become noisy when datasets include raw coordinates, identifiers, or helper columns that are meaningful for computation but not for screen-reader output. Authors need a way to omit specific dimensions while keeping the underlying data intact.


  ## Desired outcome

  Let aria label generation exclude selected dataset columns through `aria.label.data.excludeDimensionId`, so spoken descriptions can focus on the meaningful values without mutating the actual series data.


  ## Acceptance signals

  When `aria.label.data.excludeDimensionId` lists dimension indexes, those values are omitted from the generated aria label, the remaining values still appear in order, and reading back the series data shows it was not modified by aria generation.'
=============== aria-ssr-safety.yaml
title: 'fix(aria): avoid throwing error in SSR mode'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Teams using ECharts for server-side rendering or prerendered output expect accessibility features to be safe to enable outside the browser. Right now aria processing can throw in SSR environments because DOM-only behavior is assumed even when no browser element exists.


  ## Desired outcome

  Make aria support safe in SSR mode so enabling accessibility metadata does not crash chart generation when ECharts is rendered without a live browser DOM.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Charts configured with aria can be created in server-rendered environments without throwing, browser rendering keeps its current accessibility behavior, and the fix does not require users to disable aria as a workaround.'
=============== aria-test-20218.yaml
title: 'test(aria): fix test case of #20218'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  The automated coverage for aria column exclusion needs to reflect the public option structure that users are supposed to configure. This is test-maintenance work, not a change to chart behavior.


  ## Desired outcome

  Update the regression test so it validates the supported public contract at `aria.label.data.excludeDimensionId`, while keeping the existing user-facing aria behavior and data-integrity expectations unchanged.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The regression test exercises `aria.label.data.excludeDimensionId`, still confirms excluded columns disappear from the generated aria label, still confirms source data is left untouched, and no runtime feature change is introduced by the test update itself.'
=============== axis-custom-values.yaml
title: 'feat(axis): add `customValues` option to customize axis tick/label positions'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Chart authors sometimes need ticks and labels at hand-picked positions rather than at the axis scale’s automatically generated stops, for example when highlighting irregular milestones or business-specific checkpoints. Today this usually requires workarounds that can desynchronize labels from ticks.


  ## Desired outcome

  Allow both axis ticks and axis labels to opt into explicit positions through `customValues`, so authors can declare the exact values to show while still using the normal axis rendering pipeline.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Providing `customValues` on the tick or label configuration renders marks at the requested values, time axes handle those custom positions correctly, and charts that rely on automatic tick generation keep their current behavior.'
=============== axis-ticks-grid-overflow.yaml
title: 'fix(axis): fix ticks overflowing grid area with dataZoom'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  When dataZoom is applied, axis ticks near the visible edges can extend beyond the grid area and make a chart look visually broken even though the zoomed range itself is valid. Authors expect clipped or bounded ticks that stay inside the plotting region.


  ## Desired outcome

  Keep axis ticks contained within the grid when dataZoom changes the visible window, so zoomed charts look clean at the edges instead of drawing tick marks outside the plot area.


  ## Acceptance signals

  After zooming, edge ticks no longer overflow beyond the grid boundary, normal axis-tick rendering is preserved inside the plot, and unaffected non-zoomed charts keep their current appearance.'
=============== bar-bordercolor-large-data.yaml
title: 'fix(bar): fix borderColor hides bar color with large data'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Large bar-series rendering can lose the bar fill when `borderColor` is configured, making bars appear incorrectly outlined or visually empty. This is especially noticeable in dense charts where the large-data path is chosen automatically.


  ## Desired outcome

  Fix the large-data bar rendering path so `borderColor` does not hide the bar’s actual fill color.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Bars rendered through the large-data path keep their fill color even when `borderColor` is set, border styling still applies as expected, and standard bar rendering remains unchanged.'
=============== bigint-data-handling.yaml
title: 'fix(data): avoid crashing with BigInt values'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Some chart authors pass data that includes JavaScript `BigInt` values from upstream business logic or preprocessing steps. Instead of gracefully interpreting or rejecting that input, ECharts can crash during value detection and parsing, taking down the whole chart render.


  ## Desired outcome

  Make data ingestion robust when `BigInt` values are present so charts no longer throw during value parsing, and users can either render supported numeric content or get normal downstream handling instead of a hard crash.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Supplying data that contains `BigInt` no longer causes an immediate exception in the parsing pipeline, and other supported numeric data paths continue to behave exactly as before.'
=============== boxplot-encode-category-axis.yaml
title: 'fix(boxplot): correctly handle `series.encode` with category axis'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Boxplot charts can be driven from datasets and `series.encode`, but when a category axis is involved the encoded dimensions may be interpreted incorrectly. The result is a valid option that renders with misplaced or missing statistical boxes.


  ## Desired outcome

  Make boxplot series honor `series.encode` correctly on category axes so dataset-driven configurations map categories and box statistics to the intended dimensions.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A boxplot backed by dataset plus `series.encode` renders the expected categories and box values on a category axis, the encoded mapping no longer breaks the series, and existing boxplots without encode keep their current behavior.'
=============== calendar-label-silent.yaml
title: 'feat(calendar): add `silent` option for `dayLabel`/`monthLabel`/`yearLabel`'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  A chart author using the calendar coordinate system may want the day, month, or year labels to serve as static annotation rather than interactive elements. Today those labels still participate in pointer interaction, which can interfere with hover behavior on the actual calendar data and make embedded dashboards feel unexpectedly clickable.

  ## Desired outcome

  Calendar label interaction should be configurable independently for `dayLabel`, `monthLabel`, and `yearLabel`. When a user sets `silent: true` on any of those label configs, the corresponding rendered text should ignore pointer events while preserving the existing visual styling and positioning.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Authors can set `dayLabel.silent`, `monthLabel.silent`, and `yearLabel.silent` directly in the calendar option, and each one takes effect on its own. With `silent: true`, the label remains visible but no longer behaves like an interactive graphic element; with the option omitted or false, existing behavior stays unchanged.

  '
=============== candlestick-non-normal-states.yaml
title: 'fix(candlestick): add back missing support for non-normal states since v5.0.0'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Candlestick charts support emphasis, blur, and select-style visual states, and users expect those non-normal states to continue working consistently across major versions. Since v5.0.0 some of that state handling was lost, so interactive styling no longer responds correctly.


  ## Desired outcome

  Restore the missing non-normal state support for candlestick series so hover, selection, and related state-based visuals behave again the way chart authors expect.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Candlestick items respond correctly in non-normal states, state-specific styling takes effect again without breaking normal rendering, and existing candlestick options keep their prior semantics.'
=============== custom-renderitem-compoundpath.yaml
title: 'feat(custom): support compoundPath in custom series renderItem'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Custom-series authors sometimes need to return a composed path made from several subpaths as a single logical drawing element. Today `compoundPath` is not supported in `renderItem`, which blocks reusable vector shapes that are straightforward in lower-level graphics APIs.


  ## Desired outcome

  Support `compoundPath` as a valid custom-series element type so `renderItem` can return grouped path geometry in one element definition, provided `shape.paths` is supplied.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A custom series can return a `compoundPath` element from `renderItem`, `shape.paths` is honored when constructing the final graphic, and invalid compound definitions still fail clearly instead of silently misrendering.'
=============== custom-series-installer.yaml
title: 'feat(custom): use installer for reusable custom series'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Reusable custom series should integrate like other chart types so wrapper libraries and modular builds can register them through the standard installation flow. This is an API ergonomics improvement for developers building on top of ECharts.


  ## Desired outcome

  Provide installer-based registration for reusable custom series so they can be added through the normal modular setup path rather than special-case wiring.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A reusable custom series can be registered through the standard installer flow, modular imports stay consistent with other chart features, and existing custom-series usage keeps working.'
=============== dark-legend-page-text.yaml
title: 'fix(theme): fix legend page text color in dark mode'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  In dark mode, legend pagination text can retain an incorrect color that reduces contrast and readability against the theme background. Users experience this as a theme inconsistency in otherwise polished dark dashboards.


  ## Desired outcome

  Fix dark-theme legend page text coloring so paged legends remain readable and visually consistent with the rest of the dark theme.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Legend page text in dark mode uses an appropriate readable color, pagination controls stay visible against the dark background, and light-theme behavior is unchanged.'
=============== datazoom-handlelabel-show.yaml
title: 'feat(dataZoom): new option handleLabel.show'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

=============== datazoom-movehandler-cursor.yaml

=============== forked-workflow-deps.yaml

=============== gauge-negative-z2.yaml

=============== geojson-region-styling-2.yaml
title: 'feat(geo): support styling region in original GeoJSON data'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

The initial GeoJSON styling support still leaves gaps in those map-series flows, especially when a region only exists in the source map and not in user-supplied series data.

  ## Desired outcome

  GeoJSON-defined region styling should become a first-class default across map usage, not just a geo-view special case. If a feature provides `properties.echartsStyle`, that style should flow into both `geo.regions` and `series.map` region models, including regions that need to be synthesized into the data so name-based lookup, rendering, and labels all remain complete.

  ## Acceptance signals

  A `series.map` can pick up `properties.echartsStyle` from the original GeoJSON even when the author did not manually add a matching data item for that region. The style participates in the normal region model pipeline instead of being a one-off view patch, so map rendering, labels, and region lookup stay consistent with other region options.

  '
=============== geojson-region-styling.yaml
title: 'feat(geo): support styling region in original GeoJSON data'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Teams who maintain their own GeoJSON files often want the map source itself to carry default presentation rules for specific regions, instead of forcing every chart option to restate those styles. At the moment, styling embedded directly in the GeoJSON is ignored, which makes shared map assets harder to reuse across multiple visualizations.

  ## Desired outcome

  When a GeoJSON region includes an `echartsStyle` property in its feature properties, ECharts should treat that as the region''s default styling for geo rendering. This should let authors ship map-specific visual defaults inside the original GeoJSON while still allowing chart configuration to build on top of those defaults where appropriate.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Region-level styles declared in GeoJSON `properties.echartsStyle` are reflected when the map is rendered through geo-based views, without requiring duplicate style configuration in every chart option. Existing GeoJSON files that do not define `echartsStyle` continue to render exactly as before.

  '
=============== georoam-totalzoom-event.yaml
title: 'feat(geo): add `totalZoom` parameter for the `georoam` event'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Applications that react to map zooming often need the cumulative zoom level, not just the latest roam gesture, in order to coordinate labels, overlays, or linked views. Today a `georoam` listener can detect that roaming happened but cannot directly read the total scale after repeated zoom operations.


  ## Desired outcome

  Expose the accumulated zoom ratio on the `georoam` event as `totalZoom` so integrators can base follow-up UI logic on the map’s current effective zoom level instead of reconstructing it themselves.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A `georoam` handler receives `totalZoom` after zoom interactions, the value tracks cumulative zoom state across successive operations, and existing roam event behavior continues to work for listeners that do not use the new field.'
=============== inversed-time-bandwidth.yaml
title: 'fix(axis): fix bar bandWidth with inversed time axis'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Bar charts on an inversed time axis can calculate the wrong `bandWidth`, which causes bar sizing and spacing to look off even when the input data and axis configuration are otherwise correct. Authors experience this as distorted geometry on a valid timeline chart.


  ## Desired outcome

  Correct bar bandwidth calculation for inversed time axes so bar width matches the actual axis interval direction and the rendered bars keep sensible spacing.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Bars on an inversed time axis render with the expected width, reversing the axis no longer distorts band sizing, and non-inversed time-axis bar charts keep their current layout.'
=============== legend-action-isolation.yaml
title: 'fix(legend): fix legend action is not isolated from other legend components'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Pages can contain multiple legend components, and actions intended for one legend should not silently affect another. Right now some legend operations leak across legend instances, causing unexpected selection changes elsewhere in the same chart.


  ## Desired outcome

  Isolate legend actions so each legend component responds only to the interactions and action payloads meant for it, even when several legends coexist in one option.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Triggering an action on one legend no longer changes unrelated legend components, targeted legend interaction still works, and existing single-legend charts behave the same as before.'
=============== line-memory-reduction.yaml
title: 'perf(line): reduce runtime memory cost'
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  Large line charts can put unnecessary pressure on the browser by holding more runtime memory than the renderer actually needs. Users feel this as slower interaction or higher memory usage rather than as a visible API problem.


  ## Desired outcome

  Reduce the runtime memory footprint of line-series rendering without changing chart appearance, public options, or event behavior.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Equivalent line charts consume less memory during rendering or interaction, visual output remains unchanged, and no public configuration changes are required from chart authors.'
=============== linked-data-npe.yaml
title: 'fix(series): avoid NPE caused by `seriesData.getLinkedData`'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Advanced charts and extensions can interact with linked data structures internally, but some series configurations hit a null-path and throw when linked data is absent. Users experience this as a broken render caused by an internal assumption rather than an invalid option they knowingly supplied.


  ## Desired outcome

  Harden series processing so code paths that consult `seriesData.getLinkedData` tolerate missing linked datasets and continue rendering safely instead of raising a null-pointer-style exception.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Series configurations that previously crashed due to missing linked data now render or degrade normally, no exception is thrown from the linked-data lookup path, and unaffected series behavior stays the same.'
=============== map-regions-silent.yaml
title: 'feat(map): support `regions[].silent` and update map data in tests'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Map authors sometimes need a region to remain visible but non-interactive, for example when a background territory should not respond to hover, selection, or tooltip behavior. ECharts already supports top-level `silent` behavior, but there is no reliable per-region contract for map and geo regions, so authors cannot selectively disable interaction on individual areas.

  ## Desired outcome

  Region configuration should support `silent` at the per-region level through `regions[].silent`, and that setting should be honored for both geo-based maps and `series.map` rendering. A region marked silent should keep its visual appearance while opting out of event handling and interactive affordances, without forcing the entire map to become non-interactive.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Authors can declare `silent` on individual entries in `regions`, and the targeted region becomes non-interactive while neighboring regions continue to respond normally. The contract applies consistently to rendered GeoJSON regions and SVG-backed regions, and map data refreshes should preserve the updated region behavior instead of losing it when the source map data changes.

  '
=============== marker-formatter-series-context.yaml
title: 'fix(marker): fix marker label formatter can''t get series information'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  When chart authors customize marker labels with formatter callbacks, they expect to receive the same series context that other formatter-based APIs expose. For mark points, lines, and areas, that context can currently be incomplete, which prevents formatter logic from reliably reading series information.


  ## Desired outcome

  Ensure marker label formatter callbacks receive the related series metadata consistently so custom label text can depend on the originating series without hacks or duplicated state.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A marker label formatter can read the expected series information when building label text, the callback contract is consistent across marker types, and existing marker rendering remains unchanged when no custom formatter is used.'
=============== markline-symboloffset-2d-array.yaml
title: 'fix(type): markLine `symbolOffset` can be a 2d array for both symbols'
category: bugfix

  TypeScript users configuring mark lines may want separate offsets for the symbols at each end, but the current type definition can reject valid configurations even though the renderer supports them. This creates unnecessary friction in strongly typed projects.

  Update the public type contract so markLine `symbolOffset` accepts a 2D array when authors need to specify offsets for both symbols independently.


  ## Acceptance signals

  TypeScript accepts markLine configurations where `symbolOffset` is expressed as separate offset pairs for the two end symbols, existing simpler `symbolOffset` forms remain valid, and runtime chart behavior is unchanged.'
=============== master-into-v6.yaml

=============== minmax-sampling-behavior.yaml
title: 'fix(sample): fix minmax sampling behaviour'

requirement: '## Context

  ## Desired outcome

  Fix `minmax` sampling so the reduced series preserves the intended minimum and maximum behavior within each sampling bucket, especially around edge cases where the previous logic selected the wrong point order or values.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A line using `minmax` sampling retains the visible peaks and troughs expected from the source data, the sampled output is stable in the previously failing scenario, and other sampling modes continue to behave as before.'
=============== npm-package-ignore-files.yaml

=============== pictorial-zero-value-flipping.yaml
title: 'fix(pictorial): fix zero value flipping for different axes'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

After the earlier zero-value fix, some axis combinations still render a flipped symbol when the chart changes between horizontal and vertical layouts or uses inverse axes, so the same data can look wrong depending on orientation.

  Zero-valued pictorial bars should keep a stable, sensible symbol direction across horizontal and vertical charts, including inverse-axis layouts. A value of zero must no longer trigger an accidental flip simply because the axis orientation or inversion changes.

Non-zero pictorial bars continue to render with their existing direction logic, and the fix applies equally to custom image symbols and path-based symbols.

  '
=============== pictorialbar-zero-symbol-flip.yaml
title: 'fix(pictorialBar): symbol should not flip with zero data'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Keep pictorial-bar symbols from flipping when the data value is zero so orientation stays stable across zero-valued points.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A zero-value pictorial bar preserves the expected symbol direction, nearby positive or negative values still render with their intended orientation rules, and zero no longer introduces a special-case flip.'
=============== pie-empty-circle-endangle.yaml
title: 'fix(pie): fix `endAngle` is not applied on the empty circle'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

This makes dashboards look inconsistent whenever a dataset is temporarily empty.


  ## Desired outcome

  When a pie series renders its empty-circle state, the placeholder should honor the same `endAngle` setting that a normal pie would use so partial-ring designs keep their intended shape even with no slices to draw.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A chart configured with a non-default `endAngle` shows the empty circle with the matching arc extent rather than a full ring, and switching between empty and non-empty data keeps the visual geometry consistent.'
=============== pie-label-visibility.yaml
title: 'fix(pie): fix some labels may not show'

=============== polar-coordinate-clipping.yaml
title: 'fix(polar): fix unexpected clipping in polar coordinate'

=============== reusable-custom-series.yaml
title: 'feat(custom): reusable custom series'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Support a reusable payload on custom series through `itemPayload`, and expose the same object on `renderItem` params so extensions and higher-level wrappers can share contextual data cleanly across item rendering.

=============== roamcontrollerhost-import-path.yaml
title: 'fix(roam): fix RoamControllerHost importing path'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Correct the `RoamControllerHost` import path so the relevant code compiles and resolves cleanly without changing any runtime roaming behavior.

  The affected module builds without path-resolution errors, `RoamControllerHost` is imported from the correct public location, and chart interaction behavior remains unchanged.'
=============== sankey-border-radius.yaml
title: 'feat(sankey): add `itemStyle.borderRadius` option for sankey series'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  ## Desired outcome

  Allow sankey series styling to honor `itemStyle.borderRadius` so node rectangles can render with rounded corners when authors opt in, while existing charts keep their current appearance by default.

  Setting `itemStyle.borderRadius` on a sankey series produces visibly rounded node corners, the option behaves like other ECharts radius-style controls, and leaving it unset preserves the current rectangular rendering.'
=============== sankey-undefined-options.yaml
title: 'fix(sankey): avoid throwing errors when the `links` / `nodes` / `levels` option is undefined'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Applications sometimes build sankey options incrementally, and optional arrays such as `links`, `nodes`, or `levels` may be undefined until later. ECharts should not crash just because those optional fields are temporarily absent.
