  Handle missing sankey `links`, `nodes`, and `levels` inputs defensively so the chart no longer throws when those option fields are undefined.

  A sankey option with undefined `links`, `nodes`, or `levels` no longer raises an exception, normal sankey rendering still works when those arrays are provided, and authors do not need to add dummy empty arrays solely to avoid crashes.'
=============== seriesdata-rawindexof-npe.yaml
title: 'fix(data): fix potential NPE in the `SeriesData#rawIndexOf` function'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  A developer using ECharts internals or extension code can end up calling `SeriesData#rawIndexOf` in situations where the requested dimension does not have an inverted index. Instead of failing gracefully, that lookup can crash the chart pipeline with a null-pointer style error before the caller has any chance to recover.

  ## Desired outcome

  `SeriesData#rawIndexOf` should be safe to call even when the requested dimension is missing from the inverted-index map. In that case it should behave like an unsuccessful lookup rather than a hard failure, so downstream code can continue handling the result normally.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Calling `SeriesData#rawIndexOf` with a dimension that has no inverted index must not throw in production execution. The method should return the same "not found" result it already uses for missing values, namely `INDEX_NOT_FOUND`, so callers see a consistent contract instead of an exception.

  '
=============== splitline-min-max-lines.yaml
title: 'feat(axis): add `showMinLine` / `showMaxLine` option for `splitLine`'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  ## Desired outcome

  Add `showMinLine` and `showMaxLine` to split-line configuration so chart authors can independently control whether the minimum and maximum boundary lines are rendered.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Turning on `showMinLine` or `showMaxLine` renders only the requested boundary split lines, existing split-line behavior remains unchanged when the options are absent, and authors can combine them for both ends when needed.'
=============== stepped-line-area-nulls.yaml
title: 'fix(line): fix areaStyle skewing in stepped line series and incorrect connectNull behavior'

  Stepped line charts with area fills can render distorted polygons, and series that combine stepped lines with null data may connect points in ways authors did not intend. The result is a visibly wrong chart even though the series option is valid.

  Fix stepped line rendering so `areaStyle` follows the step geometry correctly and `connectNull` respects gaps in the same way users expect from the stepped path, including edge cases where null values sit near step transitions.

=============== sunburst-relative-focus.yaml
title: 'feat(sunburst): add new emphasis focus strategy `''relative''` for highlighting ancestor and descendant nodes'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

=============== time-meridian-template.yaml
title: 'feat(time): add meridian template {a}/{A}'

=============== tooltip-legend-name-xss.yaml
title: 'fix(tooltip): fix tooltip XSS issue when legend name is HTML string'

=============== tooltip-lineheight-default.yaml

=============== treemap-custom-cursor.yaml

=============== typescript-35-compatibility-tests.yaml

title: 'fix(visualMap): fix cursor is still pointer when `selectedMode` is disabled'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

Right now the control still advertises itself as clickable: hovering its pieces shows a pointer cursor even though clicking does nothing, which is misleading in polished analytical UIs.

  ## Desired outcome

  A piecewise visualMap with `selectedMode: false` should behave as a non-interactive display element, not as a disabled button that still looks active. Its symbols and labels should stop presenting click affordances while the normal selectable modes continue to behave exactly as they do today.

  ## Acceptance signals

  When `selectedMode` is enabled, hovering the visualMap still shows the interactive cursor and selection behavior is unchanged. #!/bin/bash
# usage: commit_req.sh <slug> <file1> [file2...]
# Serialized (flock) per-requirement commit: stages ONLY the given paths.
if [ $# -lt 2 ]; then echo "usage: commit_req.sh <slug> <paths...>" >&2; exit 2; fi
slug="$1"; shift
cd /workspace || exit 1
exec flock /tmp/echarts-git.lock /bin/bash -c '
  set -o pipefail
  slug="$1"; shift
  cd /workspace || exit 1
  if ! git diff --cached --quiet; then
    echo "WARNING: index was not clean before staging; aborting to avoid cross-contamination" >&2
    git diff --cached --name-only >&2
    exit 4
  fi
  git add -- "$@" || exit 5
  git diff --cached --binary > "requirement_patches/$slug.diff" || exit 6
  if [ ! -s "requirement_patches/$slug.diff" ]; then
    echo "ERROR: empty patch for $slug (no changes in: $*)" >&2
    git reset -q
    exit 3
  fi
  git add -- "requirement_patches/$slug.diff"
  git commit -q -m "impl: $slug" || exit 7
  echo "COMMITTED $slug ($(git rev-parse --short HEAD))"
' _ "$slug" "$@"
EOF
chmod +x /tmp/commit_req.sh && echo ok

content.text: Good — faithful upstream-style fix. Let me prepare the follow-up fix helper while the last clusters finish.

input.command:
cat > /tmp/fix_req.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
# usage: fix_req.sh <slug> <file1> [file2...]
# Follow-up fix for an ALREADY-committed requirement: appends the extra diff to the
# existing requirement_patches/<slug>.diff and commits (serialized with flock).
if [ $# -lt 2 ]; then echo "usage: fix_req.sh <slug> <paths...>" >&2; exit 2; fi
slug="$1"; shift
cd /workspace || exit 1
exec flock /tmp/echarts-git.lock /bin/bash -c '
  slug="$1"; shift
  cd /workspace || exit 1
  if ! git diff --cached --quiet; then
    echo "WARNING: index not clean; aborting" >&2; git diff --cached --name-only >&2; exit 4
  fi
  git add -- "$@" || exit 5
  tmp=$(mktemp)
  git diff --cached --binary > "$tmp" || exit 6
  if [ ! -s "$tmp" ]; then echo "ERROR: no changes to commit for $slug" >&2; git reset -q; rm -f "$tmp"; exit 3; fi
  { echo ""; echo "# --- follow-up fix for '"'"'$slug'"'"' ---"; cat "$tmp"; } >> "requirement_patches/$slug.diff"
  rm -f "$tmp"
  git add -- "requirement_patches/$slug.diff"
  git commit -q -m "impl: $slug" || exit 7
  echo "FIX COMMITTED $slug ($(git rev-parse --short HEAD))"
' _ "$slug" "$@"
EOF
chmod +x /tmp/fix_req.sh && echo ok && ls requirement_patches/*.diff | wc -l
